column1: # boru Language Specification: Block scopes (design/IMMUTABLE-DEF.1.md §2.1, phase 2)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# A code body a word runs — an `if` or `case` arm, an `if` or `while`
# condition, a `case` scrutinee, a `for` or `while` body, a callback body —
# is a BLOCK scope, live for one execution of the body: a `def` inside it
# binds a block local that ends with the block, and the enclosing binding,
# or none, is what a read after the block sees. `var NAME v` over a var
# visible in the enclosing scope ASSIGNS that cell and binds nothing, which
# is how a block updates state. `do`'s body is transparent by ruling (#11);
# paren groups and literals are not scopes. The check pass warns
# `shadow_rebind` on the counter shape — a block-local def whose value
# reads the very name it shadows.
# The compiled lane: a block-local def that shadows an enclosing binding
# declines compilation until the compiler's own block scopes land (phase
# 2's second step), so those rows run interpreted there, by the ledger
# (test/go/langspec/compile_failures.tsv); the var spellings compile.
# §1  loop bodies
def n 0 for 3 [def n (n add 1)] n
column3: the counter shape: the body's def is a block-local shadow that read the n it shadows; the enclosing n is unchanged

column1: var n 0 for 3 [var n (n add 1)] n
column3: …the intended spelling: the body assigns the enclosing var

column1: def t 0 each [def t (t add 1) t] [1 2 3] t
column3: each element's body shadows t afresh and reads the enclosing 0

column1: var t 0 each [var t (t add 1) t] [1 2 3] t
column3: …the var spelling accumulates across the elements

column1: for 2 [def x 9] x
column3: a loop body's def ends with the iteration: nothing is bound after the loop

column1: def i 0 while [i lt 2] [def i (i add 1) i]
column3: a while body whose def shadows the condition's name never advances it: the loop runs until the step budget ends it

column1: var i 0 while [i lt 2] [var i (i add 1) i]
column3: …the var spelling advances the condition's cell

column1: def s 0 for 3 [def s (s add i)] s
column3: a shadow that reads the loop index and the enclosing s: still a block local

column1: # §2  branch arms and conditions
if true [def w 1] [def w 2] w
column3: the arm's w ended with the arm

column1: def w (if true [1] [2]) w
column3: …the intended spelling binds the branch value

column1: def z 1 if true [def z 9 z] [0] z
column3: the arm reads its own shadow; after the arm the enclosing z stands

column1: var z 1 if true [var z 9 z] [0] z
column3: …the var spelling assigns the enclosing cell from the arm

column1: def x 1 if [def x 5 true] [x] [3] x
column3: a condition is a block too: its def shadows for the condition alone, so the arm and the read after see the enclosing x

column1: if [def y 5 true] [2] [3] y
column3: …a fresh condition def ends with the condition

column1: var x 1 if [var x 5 true] [x] [3] x
column3: …a var assignment in the condition stands for the arm and after

column1: def x 1 case [def x 5 x] [5 'five' 'other'] x
column3: a case scrutinee is a block: it dispatches on its own shadow and leaves the enclosing x

column1: def x 1 case 5 [5 [def x 7 x] 'other'] x
column3: a case arm is a block (the matched value stays beneath the arm's result, as case leaves it)

column1: def k 0 while [def j (k add 1) (j lt 3)] [1 break] k
column3: a while condition's def ends with the round; the body's break ends the loop and discards the round's value

column1: if true [def h 5 [h]] [0]
column3: a container literal the arm leaves is evaluated before the arm's block closes: it reads the arm's own local

column1: if true [def h 5 {a: h} 1] [0]
column3: …a map literal too, with the rest of the arm's residual untouched

column1: def w (if true [def h 5 [h]] [0]) w
column3: …and inside a paren group the collected value is the evaluated list

column1: if true [def r {ok:true v:2} if (r.ok) [{v:(r.v) w:[(r.v)]}] [0]] [0]
column3: …and a nested arm's literal that reaches INTO the enclosing arm's local (a dot access, not a bare word) is evaluated before that arm's block closes

column1: if true [def h 5 if true [`v=${h}`] [0]] [0]
column3: …a template string's hole over the local likewise

column1: # §3  do is transparent, frames shadow
do [def q 5] q
column3: do's body is not a block (#11): its def reaches the enclosing scope

column1: def t 0 for 3 [do [def t 5]] t
column3: …but a do inside a loop body binds in the BODY's block, which ends with the iteration

column1: def r 1 def h fn [[] [Integer] [def r 2 r]] (h) r
column3: a fn body shadows a module value and the module binding stands after the call

column1: def g fn [[x:Any] [Integer] [x add 100]] if true [def g fn [[x:Any] [Integer] [x add 1]] (g 1)] [0] g 1
column3: an arm's fn def shadows an enclosing fn inside the arm and the enclosing fn dispatches after it

column1: # §4  types end with their scope
each [def ZB (Integer gt 0) 7] [1 2]
column3: a type minted per element is retired with the element's block, so the next element mints it again

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def T (class {}) n]] f 1 f 2
column3: a type minted per call is retired with the frame: the second call's mint finds the name free

column1: each [def ZB (Integer gt 0) 7] [1] def ZB Integer 3 is ZB
column3: …and the name is free for a module def after the loop

column1: # §5  unwinding closes the block
def t 0 do [for 3 [def t 9 raise 'x']] error [drop 1] t
column3: a raise inside a loop body: the trapped error leaves the body's block closed and the enclosing t standing

column1: def t 0 do [if true [def t 9 raise 'x'] []] error [drop 1] t
column3: …and an arm's block, raised out of before its end

column1: var s 0 for 5 [def k i if (k eq 2) [break] [] var s (s add k)] s
column3: a break abandons the iteration and its block; the var assignments before it stand

column1: # §6  the check pass
import "boru:vm" (Vm.check "def n 0 for 3 [def n (n add 1)] n").warnings
column3: the counter shape warns shadow_rebind: the block-local def read the name it shadows

column1: import "boru:vm" (Vm.check "def n 0 for 3 [def n 5 n] n").warnings
column3: a plain shadow that reads nothing it shadows is no warning

column1: import "boru:vm" (Vm.check "var n 0 for 3 [var n (n add 1)] n").warnings
column3: the var spelling is what the warning asks for

column1: import "boru:vm" (Vm.check "if true [def w 1] [] w").errors
column3: a read after the arm of the arm's own name is the undefined word it is
